t:
Section 907 of title 10, United States Code (article 107 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended to read as follows:“§ 907. Art. 107. False official statements; false swearing“(a) False Official Statements.—Any person subject to this chapter who, with intent to deceive—“(1) signs any false record, return, regulation, order, or other official document, knowing it to be false; or“(2) makes any other false official statement knowing it to be false;shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.“(b) False Swearing.—Any person subject to this chapter—“(1) who takes an oath that—“(A) is administered in a matter in which such oath is required or authorized by law; and“(B) is administered by a person with authority to do so; and“(2) who, upon such oath, makes or subscribes to a statement;if the statement is false and at the time of taking the oath, the person does not believe the statement to be true, shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.”
.

fable.w: The section amends the UCMJ to define the offenses of false official statements and false swearing, punishable by court-martial. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" signals rulemaking, but here it is only one of the kinds of document a person may falsely sign, not a grant of rulemaking authority. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: signs any false record, return, regulation, order, or other official document, knowing it to be false

opus.w: This section defines military crimes (false official statements and false swearing) and says they are punished as a court-martial directs. It has no comment period, rulemaking authority, hearing, advisory body or consultation with non-federal parties. The word "regulation" only names a kind of document that might be falsified, and a court-martial is an internal military justice proceeding, not outside participation in a federal decision.
opus.b: The section amends UCMJ Article 107, which defines false official statements and false swearing as offenses punishable by court-martial. One could misread it as participation because of the word "regulation" and the mention of court-martial proceedings. But "regulation" only appears as an example of an official document that someone might falsify; the section does not authorize anyone to write a rule. A court-martial is a military justice proceeding inside the federal government. It does not bring outsiders into a federal policy decision or give anyone a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines criminal offenses (false official statements and false swearing) under the Uniform Code of Military Justice and prescribes punishment by court-martial. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in a federal decision-making process. The actors involved are military personnel and military judicial bodies, all of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Any person subject to this chapter who, with intent to deceive—“(1) signs any false record, return, regulation, order, or other official document, knowing it to be false; or“(2) makes any other false official statement knowing it to be false;shall be punished as a court-martial may direct.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "person with authority to do so" who administers the oath is an outside party, or that the court-martial process involves public participation. However, the text defines criminal offenses within the military justice system. The "person with authority" is a military officer (inside the government), and the court-martial is an internal military judicial proceeding. There is no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private organizations) in the decision-making process described here. The section merely defines punishable conduct.
